questions.q: How does this teaching version's architecture differ from a production AMM like Uniswap V2?
options: It collapses the factory, pair contract, and router into one single SimplePool contract
It uses three separate factories instead of one
It requires a router for every single swap
It has no architectural differences from a production AMM
questions.explain: A production AMM splits responsibilities across a factory, a pair contract, and often a router; this teaching version deliberately collapses all of that into one readable SimplePool contract.

questions.q: Why does the first liquidity depositor's minted share amount use sqrt(amtA * amtB) instead of a ratio against existing reserves?
options: Because there's no existing reserve ratio yet to match, since the pool is empty
Because square roots are required by the Solidity compiler for all uint256 math
Because the first depositor always receives zero shares
Because it reduces gas costs compared to any other formula
questions.explain: With totalShares at zero, there's no existing price ratio to proportion against, so the contract uses sqrt(amtA * amtB) to set the pool's starting price from the first deposit.

questions.q: In swapAforB, what does the checks-effects-interactions pattern mean in practice?
options: Reserves update before the outbound token transfer, so external calls happen last
The function checks the caller's identity before allowing any swap
All interactions happen before any state is read
The pattern only applies to removeLiquidity, not to swaps
questions.explain: swapAforB updates reserveA and reserveB (the contract's own state) before calling tokenB.transfer (the external interaction), which is exactly the checks-effects-interactions ordering that blocks reentrancy.

questions.q: Which of these is explicitly flagged in this lesson as a known simplification/gap in the swap function, not something quietly left unmentioned?
options: The absence of a minAmountOut slippage parameter
The use of Solidity version numbers
The presence of two separate ERC-20 tokens
The use of a mapping for storing reserves
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly calls out the missing minAmountOut slippage parameter as a known gap, one that Lesson 6's security review picks back up directly — rather than leaving it unstated.

questions.q: How does this contract track each liquidity provider's claim on the pool?
options: With a plain mapping(address => uint256), not a minted ERC-20 LP token
By minting a separate transferable ERC-20 LP token, exactly like a production AMM
It doesn't track individual claims at all
By storing claims in an off-chain database
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that this teaching version uses a plain mapping for shares instead of minting a real transferable LP token, trading that feature away for a contract that's easier to read in full.
